Zelensky Meets Kellogg, Offers to Buy Patriot Missiles — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with retired US Lieutenant General and former presidential envoy Keith Kellogg in Kyiv on Aug. 22. Kyiv Seeks to Renegotiate EU Agricultural Export Quotas in September — Ukraine intends to renegotiate its tariff-free agricultural export quotas with the EU starting in September. Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotsky urged industry representatives to provide data to support demands for increased quotas on sensitive items like sugar and bioethanol. The incident follows a series of recent airspace violations in the region. Moldovan Preside

The aid includes €50 million ($58.4 million) for humanitarian support (focusing on generators) and €10 million ($11.7 million) for the NATO Comprehensive Assistance Package. Ukraine Destroys Su-24M at Saky, Hits Primorsko-Akhtarsk Airfield — President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed on Aug. 22 that Ukrainian forces have destroyed a Russian Su-24M aircraft and four pieces of equipment at the Saky airfield in Crimea, as well as drone relay stations in the Bryansk region. EU Raises Ukrainian Flag in Brussels Ahead of Independence Day — The European Commission raised the Ukrainian flag in Brussels on Aug. 21 ahead of Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day, with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stating that Ukraine will take its “rightful place” in the Union. It Is Not Putin’s War. It’s Russia’s — Those who bet that Russians would be appalled at the slaughter they inflicted on Ukraine have lost the wager. Four years of Ukrainian suffering and senseless meatgrinder tactics have not shaken Russian society. Disruption to Russian comfort is all that’s made a mark.

Russia Strikes Boryspil and Zaporizhzhia, Killing 5 People — Russian forces launched multiple deadly strikes across Ukraine on Saturday, Aug. 22. A ballistic missile strike in the Boryspil district of the Kyiv region killed two people and injured five, damaging local infrastructure. In a separate attack, seven strikes on the Zaporizhzhia district killed three people and injured 15, including a child.

Poland Maintains Long‑Term Legal, Financial Protections for 1.7 Million Ukrainian Refugees — Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion, Poland has provided legal and financial protection to 1.7 million Ukrainian refugees, the Polish Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported. According to the ministry, an unprecedented 77% of Poles actively participated in helping Ukrainian refugees, with 7% taking them into their own homes. Drones Attack Yeysk Seaport in Russia’s Krasnodar Region — Unidentified drones attacked the Yeysk seaport in Russia’s Krasnodar region on Saturday, Aug. 22, according to reports and eyewitness videos showing smoke in the port area. Preliminary information suggests a vessel may have caught fire.

Russian Strikes Damage Infrastructure and Utilities in Odesa Region, Injuring 1 — Russian overnight strikes on the Odesa region damaged transport, industrial, energy, and residential infrastructure, leaving one person injured and causing power and water outages, according to Regional Military Administration Head Oleh Kiper. The Rozdilna railway station, a five-story residential building, and a sports facility were among the targets hit. The strikes were part of a massive nationwide barrage invol

Who Is Lev Shlosberg, the Russian Politician Jailed for Opposing Russia’s War? — Russian opposition politician Lev Shlosberg has been sentenced to 11 years and one month in a penal colony over anti-war statements and a social-media repost. His record stretches from exposing the covert deployment of Russian paratroopers to Ukraine in 2014 to demanding an immediate ceasefire after the full-scale invasion. His radical pacifism has also drawn strong criticism from Ukrainians and other Kremlin oppone

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul Arrives in Kyiv — German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived in Kyiv on Saturday, Aug. 22, to demonstrate continued support ahead of Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day. Wadephul emphasized the need for Europe to remain united and highlighted a joint effort with France to petition for international assistance to protect Ukraine’s critical infrastructure before winter.

Modern Independent Ukraine at 35: Achievements and Problems — During a recent cultural festival on the grounds of Kyiv’s St. Sophia’s Cathedral, prominent diplomats, dissidents, writers and cultural figures discussed Ukraine’s key achievements and problems.

Ukraine Appoints 16 New Judges to High Anti-Corruption Court — President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed 16 new judges to the High Anti-Corruption Court (HACC) on Aug. 21, assigning 11 to the first instance and five to the Appeals Chamber. HACC Chief of Staff Bohdan Kryklyvenko noted that one additional candidate’s paperwork was delayed, while two existing judges are finishing pending cases before officially joining the Appeals Chamber. The appointments fulfill a delayed structural benchmark under

Ukraine Downs 182 Drones and Missiles in Mass Russian Attack — The Ukrainian Air Force reported intercepting 182 drones out of 217 launched, along with three Kh-31P/Kh-59 aviation missiles and six “Banderol” munitions during an early Saturday morning attack. Russian forces targeted the Kyiv and Odesa regions utilizing Iskander-M and S-400 ballistic missiles, jet-powered Shaheds, and decoy drones launched from multiple Russian regions and occupied territories. Officials recorded direct hits at 41

Russian Emigration Interest Doubles Amid Fears of Mobilization This Fall — Russian emigration consultancy organizations report a significant surge in relocation inquiries since July, driven by fears of a new military mobilization this fall. Projects such as Relocats and Ark noted up to a 1.7-fold increase in daily requests, with citizens primarily targeting Serbia, Armenia, and Georgia. The spike in interest coincides with warnings from Ukrainian intelligence and political analysts that Moscow m

Russian Missiles Strike Kyiv Railway Facility, Killing One Worker — Russian ballistic missiles targeted a railway enterprise in Kyiv’s Darnytsia district on Aug. 22, killing an Ukrzaliznytsia foreman. The strike occurred almost simultaneously with air raid warnings, and remaining staff were evacuated after the initial impact. A separate attack damaged the Rozdilna station building in the Odesa region, though overall train operations remain unaffected.

Drones Strike Novokuibyshevsk Refinery and Ozon Hub in Samara Region — Ukrainian drone strikes targeted the Samara region on Aug. 22, causing a fire at the Novokuibyshevsk oil refinery, a Rosneft subsidiary with an 8.8-million-ton annual capacity. Reports also indicate a strike on a 75,000-square-meter fulfillment center operated by Ozon, one of Russia’s largest e-commerce platforms. The attacks follow a sustained Ukrainian campaign against Russian logistics and infrastructure, including massive

Ukraine Sanctions Five Russian Rusal Aluminum Enterprises — President Volodymyr Zelensky enacted a National Security and Defense Council decision imposing sanctions on five enterprises of the Russian aluminum group Rusal and nine associated citizens. The sanctions target major production sites in Bratsk, Sayanogorsk, and Krasnoyarsk, which import over $2.5 billion in alumina annually. Germany Weighs Closing Berlin’s ‘Russian House’ Amid Rising Hybrid Threats — Germany is considering closing Berlin’s Russian House as officials reassess agreements underpinning the center amid growing concern over Russian hybrid activity.

Shopping Mall Tragedy: Two Children Among Nine Missing After Kryvyi Rih Mall Strike Kills 16 — Nine people, including two children, remain missing after Russia’s strike on a Kryvyi Rih mall that killed at least 16 and injured 130.

Two Dead After Small Plane Crashes in Croatia’s Paklenica National Park — A small plane flying from the Czech Republic crashed in Croatia’s Paklenica National Park, killing two people, authorities said.

Russia Launches Multiple Ballistic Missiles at Kyiv, Killing One and Injuring Others — At least one person was killed and others injured as Russia launched ballistic missiles at Kyiv, sparking a warehouse fire in the Darnytskyi district.

Kyiv to Host 10 Foreign Leaders for Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day — Around 10 foreign leaders are expected in Kyiv for Ukraine’s 35th Independence Day, while the Coalition of the Willing meets to coordinate further support.

Russian Forces Launch 172 Attacks Across Front Line on Friday — Russian forces launched 172 attacks along the front line on Friday, Aug. 21, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) said. Russia also carried out 75 airstrikes using 219 guided aerial bombs (KABs), and deployed 6,571 attack drones.

Over 70% of Ukraine’s Residential Buildings Ready for 2026-27 Winter Season — Ukraine has prepared more than 70% of housing for the 2026-27 heating season, according to Minister of Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport, Mykola Kalashnyk on Friday, Aug. 21. Nearly Hr. 6.8 billion ($152 million) has been allocated for preparation works and repairs as authorities seek to protect energy infrastructure from Russian attacks.

Former Defense Minister Fedorov Considering Running for President, Sources Say — According to Ukrainska Pravda citing sources close to Fedorov, the former minister may be considering a presidential bid, following his wartime elections call on Tuesday, Aug. 18. His team also reported that he is considering backing another candidate or party, or remaining outside electoral politics while he works in the private sector.

Zelensky Informs UN Secretary-General Guterres About Russian Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky, following Russia’s massive strike on a shopping mall in his hometown of Kryvy Rih, said he spoke with UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Friday, Aug. 21. The two discussed Russia’s continued attacks on Ukraine, civilian casualties, and global food security threats.

EU Pledges Support for Ukraine’s Anti-Graft Efforts Amid New ‘Forrest Gump’ Probe — EU ambassadors met the heads of Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies, the National Anti-Corruption Bureau of Ukraine (NABU) and the Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (SAPO), in Kyiv on Friday, Aug. 21, pledging continued support for the country’s reform efforts. The meeting comes two days after a new corruption probe dubbed “Forrest Gump” targeted Sense Bank.

8,500 North Korean Troops Now in Russia, Ukraine Says — North Korea has sent a new contingent of around 8,500 troops to Russia, including approximately 400 drone operators, Ukrainian military intelligence Deputy Head Vadym Skibitskyi told CNN. The troops are expected to reinforce Russian rear positions, potentially freeing Russian forces for frontline assaults. Skibitskyi said Moscow could seek up to 50,000 additional North Korean troops, while Pyongyang is also supplying ballistic missiles and

Russia’s Shopping Mall Strike on Zelensky’s Hometown Kills 15, Injures 130 as Rescue Continues — Russia struck a shopping mall in central Ukraine’s Kryvyi Rih on Friday afternoon, killing at least 15 and injuring over 130. Officials said casualties are likely to rise as they warned of additional strikes as jet-powered drones continue circling around the city at low altitudes.

Wartime Government in Ukraine and the Zelensky-Fedorov Clash — The dismissal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and a series of corruption allegations involving figures close to Bankova have sharpened questions about whether Ukraine’s wartime centralization remains subject to meaningful constitutional checks. While martial law and postponed elections are legal, the deeper issue is whether parliament, oversight bodies and other institutions retain the power to hold the presidency accountable.

Ukrainian Authorities Detain Chornomorsk Port Official in Bribery Probe — Ukrainian authorities detained a Chornomorsk port official and an alleged intermediary over a Hr. 500,000 ($11,200) payment demanded from a contractor working on railway infrastructure at the port.

Russia Seeks New Charges Against Teenager Accused of Blowing Up FSB Building in Minecraft — Russia is seeking new charges against Nikita Uvarov, a teenager arrested in 2020 for putting up political leaflets who was subsequently accused of blowing up an FSB building in-game in preparation for real-world scenarios. The new charges were brought to him a month before he was scheduled to be released earlier this year.

NATO Military Committee to Return to Ukraine After Eight Years — Ukraine will host the NATO Military Committee in October, marking the first such visit in eight years, Ukrainian Armed Forces Commander Mykhailo Drapatyi said. Drapatyi discussed the frontline situation and Ukraine’s priorities with NATO Military Committee Chair Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, including long-range strikes, infantry tactics, battlefield robotics and air defense.

More Than 15 Explosions in 20 Minutes Rock Occupied Crimea Amid Power Outages — More than 15 explosions were reported near Simferopol amid alleged drone activity, including sightings near the Tavriyska Thermal Power Plant. Russian authorities claimed that two people were killed and six injured, while Russian-controlled utilities reported damage to energy infrastructure and power outages across the occupied peninsula.

Trump Rejects Push to Give Ukraine Starlink for Long-Range Strikes on Russia – FT — President Donald Trump has rejected Ukraine’s request to persuade Elon Musk to allow Starlink for drone strikes inside Russia, the Financial Times reported. Kyiv says the satellite network could help target Russian ballistic missile launchers more precisely as Ukraine faces dwindling Patriot interceptor stocks ahead of winter.

Suspected Russian Handguns Found Near Berlin: German Media — German security services have uncovered two handguns hidden near Berlin that they suspect were intended for Russian agents preparing “kinetic operations,” German media reported. The discovery comes amid growing concerns over Russian sabotage and assassination plots targeting Germany’s defense industry and Ukraine supporters.

Russian Social Network VK Sues Apple Over App Store Removal — VK, Russia’s largest social media conglomerate, said it has filed a lawsuit against Apple over the tech giant’s delisting of its applications in June. VK is now seeking 58 million rubles per day in damages, which include 50 million rubles for the VK platform, 3 million for the Odnolassniki network, and 5 million for the VK Music service.

Nord Stream Suspect Arrested on Set of Film About the Sabotage — A Ukrainian diver suspected by German prosecutors of helping sabotage the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022 was arrested in Pula, Croatia, while reportedly working as a consultant on a Hollywood film dramatizing the attack. The film, Snake Island, is directed by Doug Liman and stars Sean Penn and Adrien Brody. German prosecutors accuse the suspect of belonging to a group that planted explosives on the pipelines near Denmark.

Ukraine Sanctions Russia’s Hit ‘Masha and the Bear’ Cartoon — Ukraine has sanctioned the producers and distributors of the popular Russian children’s cartoon “Masha and the Bear,” paving the way for its content to be blocked and monetization restricted. Kyiv says the series is a Kremlin propaganda tool with no place on Ukrainian children’s screens.

Australia Hits Russian Man With ‘Foreign Interference’ Charges Over Plot to Infiltrate Ukrainian Military — Australia said it arrested a 27-year-old dual Australian-Russian national on “foreign interference” charges. The man is said to have received “military-style” training in Russia in 2024 before joining the Ukrainian military in March 2025 in an attempt to pass on intelligence to Russian security services.

Ukraine Planned 1,000-Drone Swarm to Paralyze Moscow Airports — Ukraine reportedly planned to unleash up to 1,000 autonomous AI-powered drones on Moscow’s airports in a single night, aiming to overwhelm air defenses, cripple flights and pressure the Kremlin back to negotiations. The operation was halted after former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov’s July departure.

Russia Deploys North Korean Ballistic Missiles Within Reach of 7 Ukrainian Regions — Russia is preparing to expand its use of North Korean ballistic missiles, with six launchers reportedly deployed in Voronezh Oblast, the ISW said. Ukrainian military intelligence said North Korea had transferred around 50 KN-23, KN-24 and upgraded KN-30 missiles to Russia by July. From Voronezh, the missiles could reach the Sumy, Kharkiv, Chernihiv, Poltava, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions.

Russia Strikes Ukraine-Moldova Border Crossing for Second Night in a Row — Russia attacked a Ukrainian border crossing with Moldova for the second night in a row, damaging infrastructure and forcing the checkpoint to close, Kyiv said. The strikes come after Moldova reported a drone entering its airspace.

‘Don’t Even Think About It’: Ex-Danish FM Warns Russia Amid NATO Drills — NATO’s Nordic allies are strengthening military readiness and air defenses as tensions with Russia persist. Former Danish Foreign Minister Jeppe Kofod urged faster defense spending, closer regional cooperation and stronger protection of critical infrastructure. He said NATO exercises near Kaliningrad demonstrate readiness to respond, while stressing continued military and air-defense support for Ukraine.

Mariupol Volunteer Safe After Risking Everything to Save Son Allegedly Threatened by Russia’s FSB — Ukrainian volunteer Mykhailo Puryshev says he is safe after traveling to Moscow to save his 18-year-old son, whom he says Russia’s FSB threatened with death or being sent to fight against Ukraine if he refused to cooperate. Puryshev has not disclosed how he escaped Russia.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Major Lukoil Refinery, Military Airfield as Russia Claims 325 UAVs Downed — Ukraine struck the Perm oil refinery and Marynovka military airfield in separate long-range attacks, Zelensky said. He also reported earlier damage to a Russian Su-34 and a facility used to prepare and launch attack drones.

Russia Unleashes 135 Drones on Ukraine, Killing 2 in Kharkiv Region and Injuring 6 in Sumy — Russia launched 135 drones at Ukraine overnight, with 107 intercepted or suppressed. Strikes damaged homes and civilian infrastructure in Sumy, where 6 were injured, while two women were killed and two people wounded in Kharkiv region.

Ex-Defense Minister Fedorov Plans US Trip for Defense Tech, Team Denies Political Meetings — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is planning a US trip focused on defense technology projects, his team says, pushing back on reports linking the visit to political outreach.

How Energy-Exporting Russia Is Turning Into a Fuel Importer – Thanks to Ukraine — Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed Russia has begun importing fuel as Ukrainian strikes disrupt refineries, squeeze gasoline supplies and force rationing.

Romania Destroys Explosive Marine Drone Near Major Black Sea Gas Project — Romania destroyed an explosive-carrying marine drone near the Neptun Deep offshore gas project after it approached critical infrastructure in the Black Sea. Kyiv told Bucharest the vessel was not Ukrainian, while Romania’s president blamed Russia.

Zelensky: Ukraine Downed 90% of Russian Cruise Missiles, Vows Long-Range Response — Ukraine intercepted about 90% of Russian cruise missiles in the overnight attack, but Zelensky said ballistic missiles remain far harder to stop and urged partners to provide more Patriot interceptors. He also pledged additional resources for Ukraine’s long-range strike capabilities.

Finland suspects Russian plane of violating its airspace — Finland’s Defense Ministry said it is investigating a suspected Russian aircraft incursion into its airspace, following similar incidents involving Russian military aircraft in May and June.

Russia Places German Journalist Michael Martens on Wanted List — Russia placed Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) correspondent Michael Martens on its Interior Ministry wanted list on Aug. 15, following his question to President Volodymyr Zelensky about increasing Russian military casualties during his meeting with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić on Aug. 8.
